item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 5
item.description:
Fifth beta. When the Teams names do not appear, Notetaker now tells you which step failed. Beta 4 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Every step that names a speaker logs.** Notetaker writes a line when it finds a Teams call, when it sees who speaks, and when it names the voices at the end. When a step fails, the line says why: no Accessibility access, no call found, a tile it does not know, no speaking ring, or cues that named nobody. The log holds counts and states, not names (D34). - **"Save diagnostics" in the menu.** It writes a folder with the app and Mac facts, the log of this run, and, while Teams runs, ten copies of the Teams window. The folder opens in the Finder. Nothing leaves the Mac: you read the files and decide what to send.
## What to try
- Record a Teams call. While somebody speaks, choose "Save diagnostics" in the menu. It takes some seconds. Send `about.txt` and `log.txt` from the folder. `teams.json` holds the names in the call and any open chat text: read it before you send it. - After Stop, choose "Save diagnostics" again. The log then also holds the naming step.
## Known gaps
- The new logging is not yet tested in a live Teams call. - Teams in a language other than English, and Teams in a web browser, give no names. The log now says so. - People who are not on the Teams stage give no speaker names. - A guest line heard through the speakers can still show as "Me".

item.title: Notetaker 0.1.0 beta 4
item.description:
Fourth beta. Notetaker now knows who you talk to in a Microsoft Teams call, and who says what. Beta 3 finds it within a day and asks to restart.
## What changed
- **Names from Teams.** During a Teams call, Notetaker reads the Teams window on your Mac. The people on the stage become the attendees of the session, and a person who joins late is added. The meeting title names a session that has no calendar event. No bot joins the call, and nothing leaves the Mac (D33). - **A name on each line.** Teams shows who speaks. Notetaker reads that once a second, and at the end it gives each line of the call audio the name of the person who spoke it. The action items in the notes now have real owners. - **Access on a click only.** Choose "Name the people in Teams calls" in the menu, then turn on Notetaker in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility. Without this access, sessions work as in beta 3. - **"Check for updates" works again after a download.** While a downloaded update waited for the restart, the menu item did nothing. It now shows the update window again.
## What to try
- Give Notetaker the Accessibility access. Record a Teams call with two colleagues. At the end, the attendees and each line of their speech carry their names, and the action items name their owners.
## Known gaps
- Tested in a live Teams call with two synthetic voices, not yet with real people. - Teams in a language other than English, and Teams in a web browser, give no names. - People who are not on the Teams stage give no speaker names. - A guest line heard through the speakers can still show as "Me".
